title: example-targets Phase 5, gate A3: example 285 (CVE-2023-34055) replay of Boot 2.7.17 and 2.7.18's WebMvcTags.method on the original JARs
description: The job runs python3 examples/tools/build.py 285 --task replay, the target route of llm-dlc/loops/example-targets.md: workflow plans the task from target.json, runtime prepares each revision by the published-artifact route (every JAR acquired from Maven Central by the sha256 its sidecar pins, refused on a mismatch; driver and adapter compiled with --release 21), runs the packet's driver over its probes in a separate JVM per revision on JDK 21 and on JDK 25, and workflow ingests the records into one format-2 receipt under receipts/replay/, reading each revision's driver lines with the packet's independent oracle (controls/oracle.py problems()). A replay decides no claim: build.py exits 0 only when the receipt's matchesExpected is true, i.e. every revision ran on both JDKs, exited 0 with structured observations, and each shows what its pair's kind expects on both JDKs alike. No proof runs. This is Phase 5 step 1's first run of a real packet through the merged infrastructure; a failure in a stream's code is a finding to fix with a reproducer. Example 285: Spring Boot's WebMvcTags.method(HttpServletRequest), the actuator's HTTP method tag, unbounded before the fix (any method string becomes a tag value) and limited to known methods after it. The release pair is v2.7.17 (2caabd06) and v2.7.18 (0c8b382d): spring-boot-actuator with its declared closure (micrometer-core 1.9.16, spring-web/webmvc/core/jcl 5.3.30, javax.servlet-api 4.0.1; 14 pinned JARs). A3 needs the vulnerable release to violate the oracle on the triggers and the fixed one to hold, with the legitimate controls retained.
expected: build.py prints '285-...: task replay: none (completed; as expected)' and exits 0: vulnerable-release violates the oracle at its trigger probes and fixed-release holds, on JDK 21 and 25 alike; a receipt under examples/285-*/receipts/replay/

resources.notes: 14 small JARs from Maven Central (a few MB), two javac runs per revision, four short JVM runs
